summary: Bourgeois Inlet light, Cape Breton: built 1902, lit 1903; wooden tower burned 1989; community-owned replica of 2003 stands at Church Point.

structures.note: 27 ft (8.2 m) from stone foundation to the vane (Department 1903); burned by the Coast Guard in June 1989 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)

structures.note: Exact replica of the 1903 tower built by the community (Rowlett; local history). The Coast Guard list gives the tower as 7.7 m.

access.note: The tower is reached across private property; LighthouseFriends suggests viewing it from the south side of the church. Rowlett: accessible at low tide, but access may be cut off at high tide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1902 Department report describes the tower as being built under contract; the 1903 report says it was put in operation at the opening of navigation in 1903. The record's 2003 build event is the replica, not the 1903 tower.

The Coast Guard list gives Iso R 4s (isophase red every four seconds, 7.1 m focal height). Rowlett describes a continuous red light of 7.5 m (25 ft) focal plane. The story gives the Coast Guard characteristic and states Rowlett's description. NSLPS gives 'Fixed White (1922)' and 'Still Operating: No', which the story does not use.
LighthouseFriends quotes the Coast Guard's reason for removing the 1903 tower (rotten stairs and frame, hazardous to maintain); the local history gives the cost of maintenance. The story gives both.

The station record says boat-only access. LighthouseFriends says the tower is reached by land across private property, and Rowlett says it is accessible at low tide. The story follows the land-access sources; the record flag is left for review.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1902 report's Bourgeois inlet entry is on p. 75 (scan 88), not p. 88; the contractor's name is printed 'Dovle' in the OCR and reads Doyle on the page image. The 1904 keeper table row (Bourgeois Inlet; Burke, Martin; appointed Dec. 1, 1902; p. 160, scan 173) was read on the page image. The salary figure in that row was not legible enough to use. The story now has chapter headings (the evidence supports a moderate story, not a thin one). 1) Edward Doyle's name is OCR'd 'Dovle' in the 1902 report; the story uses Doyle, as LighthouseFriends spells it. 2) Martin Burke is placed beside Bourgeois Inlet in the 1904 table by column position (the OCR lists 'Bourgeois Inlet. Dec. May Aug. Feb.' then 'Burke, Martin'). LighthouseFriends confirms the name and years 1902 to 1912. D. Sampson's station is not confirmed in any Department list read. 3) Dates for the 1989 burning and replacement differ: LighthouseFriends 2 June 1989; Rowlett 1989; the local history 1989; NSLPS 1990 or 1991. The story gives 1989 with NSLPS's date noted. 4) The replica year: Rowlett and the local history say 2003; a Lighthouse Digest search snippet (not read) says the divestiture was in 2004. 5) NSLPS says both 'Operating: This light is operational' and 'Still Operating: No'; the Coast Guard list (verified, Iso R 4s, 7.1 m) and Rowlett (privately maintained, active) are treated as current. Rowlett says 'continuous red light', the Coast Guard 'Iso R 4s'; the story uses the Coast Guard. 6) Record 'visit.boat_only: true' conflicts with Rowlett (accessible at low tide) and LighthouseFriends (reached by land across private property). Not changed; flagged for review. 7) The record's first_lit was null; the 1903 operation date comes from the Department's 1904 report and NSLPS. 8) NSLPS's '1922 7th order dioptric lens' and '1973 automated' entries are not used: the same page gives 'Automated by 1993', and the 1922 lens is unexplained. 9) No Chronicling America search was run for this thin station.
